questions.question: In Factorization Machines (FMs), how is the computational complexity of evaluating all pairwise feature interactions reduced from $O(k d^2)$ to $O(k d)$, where $d$ is the number of features and $k$ is the dimensionality of the factorized vectors?
options: By assuming that feature interaction vectors are sparse and setting higher-order terms to zero.
By reformulating the sum of pairwise dot products using an algebraic identity that computes the square of sums minus the sum of squares.
By projecting the input features into a low-dimensional space using Principal Component Analysis prior to calculating interactions.
By enforcing strict orthogonality constraints on the latent factor matrix during optimization.

questions.question: In Gaussian Process Regression with kernel function $K$, noise variance $\sigma_n^2$, and training data inputs $X$, what is the correct analytical expression for the predictive variance at a single unseen test point $\mathbf{x}_*$?
options: $\text{Var}(f_*) = K(\mathbf{x}_*, \mathbf{x}_*) - \mathbf{k}_*^T (K(X, X) + \sigma_n^2 I)^{-1} \mathbf{k}_*$
$\text{Var}(f_*) = K(\mathbf{x}_*, \mathbf{x}_*) + \mathbf{k}_*^T (K(X, X) - \sigma_n^2 I)^{-1} \mathbf{k}_*$
$\text{Var}(f_*) = \mathbf{k}_*^T K(X, X)^{-1} \mathbf{k}_* + \sigma_n^2$
$\text{Var}(f_*) = K(\mathbf{x}_*, \mathbf{x}_*) - \mathbf{k}_*^T K(X,X)^{-1} \mathbf{k}_* + \sigma_n^2 I$

questions.question: Which dynamic programming algorithm is used to find the single most likely sequence of hidden states (the MAP state sequence) given an observation sequence in a Hidden Markov Model (HMM)?
options: The Forward algorithm
The Baum-Welch algorithm
The Viterbi algorithm
The Backward algorithm

questions.question: In the Isolation Forest algorithm for anomaly detection, why do anomalous data points typically exhibit significantly shorter average path lengths in the isolation trees compared to normal points?
options: Anomalies have a higher local density, causing them to be isolated into leaf nodes earlier.
Anomalies are few in number and possess attribute values distinct from normal points, requiring fewer random recursive splits to be isolated.
Isolation trees utilize Euclidean distance metrics to explicitly isolate distant points at shallow tree depths.
Anomalies are systematically partitioned into root nodes during the supervised training phase.

questions.question: How does the Jensen-Shannon (JS) divergence differ fundamentally from the standard Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence between two probability distributions $P$ and $Q$?
options: JS divergence is asymmetric, whereas KL divergence is symmetric.
JS divergence can take negative values when distributions overlap significantly, whereas KL divergence is strictly non-negative.
JS divergence is valid only for discrete probability distributions, whereas KL divergence applies only to continuous distributions.
JS divergence is symmetric and bounded between 0 and 1 (when using base-2 logarithm), whereas KL divergence is asymmetric and unbounded.
